title: Introduce sequential perturbation schedule and grace-window gate
author: Maya Chen
commits: a1b2c3: add sequential perturbation harness + runner
d4e5f6: introduce grace-window gate and coordinator
i1j2k3: ci integration and smoke backfill job
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently see brittle regressions on prompt sets that only surface when multiple small perturbations are applied in sequence (e.g., punctuation->case->synonym). Existing single-perturbation probes miss these cascading failure modes. This PR adds a sequential perturbation runner and a configurable CI gate with a grace-window to reduce flapping for transient noise.

What this changes: 1) A new harness (eval-harness/hooks/sequential_perturbation.py) that composes perturbation passes into ordered schedules. Schedules are declarative (examples in examples/perturbation-configs/) and support weighted sampling, early-exit on divergence, and deterministic seeding for reproducibility. 2) A new gate (eval-harness/gates/grace_window_gate.py) which evaluates metric streams over a configurable time window and only triggers hard failures when a signal persists beyond the grace period. 3) Two new metrics: compression-aware divergence (captures structural compression differences that indicate paraphrase collapse) and token-level saliency delta (helps pinpoint where the model changed token importance after perturbations). 4) CI integration: a backfill/smoke job (ci/pipelines/eval-smokebackfill.yml) that runs the sequential schedule against recent canary snapshots and reports to the existing eval-dashboard. 5) Docs and examples for configuring schedules and gate thresholds (docs/eval/seq-perturbation.md).

Design notes: The sequential runner supports three modes: replay (deterministic order), stochastic-schedule (sampled sequences with fixed seed), and adversarial-grid (exhaustive short sequences for narrow prompt cohorts). The gate computes a rolling severity score combining metric z-scores, cohort weight, and historical stability; the grace window is expressed as x runs / y minutes threshold (configurable per-linear key). We intentionally keep the gate soft-fail by default with an optional policy to escalate to hard-fail after an extended grace period.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added (tests/test_seq_perturb.py) for schedule parsing, deterministic replay, and early-exit behavior. End-to-end smoke runs were executed against three internal canaries (conversational, summarization, code-completion) — CI artifacts show no notable latency regression (+~1.2% token processing time in worst case due to extra perturbation instrumentation). Metric-level thresholds were tuned on historical rolling windows (30d anchor) and validated against known regressions to ensure recall.

Rollout and risk mitigation: Rollout is staged. Step 1: enable pipeline in nightly smoke for opt-in teams and collect telemetry for 7 days. Step 2: enable soft gating in PR-level CI for top-10 prompt sets by volume. Step 3: enable default soft gating org-wide and add escalation policy for persistent signals. We add backfill tooling so new schedules can be re-run over last 14 days to build baselines.

Operational notes: The gate emits structured events to the eval-dashboard and attaches sample failing prompts + perturbation trace (via eval-harness/utils/trace_exporter.py). We also add a debug flag to export token-saliency diffs for investigator workflows. Compression-aware divergence uses lightweight LZ-based sketching to avoid large payloads.

Related work and references: This PR complements ENG-3421 (cohort prioritizer) by adding a failure-mode-aware probe and links to ENG-3499 (alert fusion) for escalation behavior. It is intentionally model-agnostic and works with both hosted and private eval runners.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add sequential perturbation runner + schedules
- [x] Implement grace-window gate with configurable policy
- [x] Add metric implementations and unit tests
- [x] Wire up CI smoke/backfill pipeline
- [x] Add docs and example configs
- [x] Run canary E2E smoke and tune thresholds

Notes on performance/security: No new credentials or secrets required. The runner adds modest CPU overhead during CI (increasing runtime of some eval jobs); batching and caching are preserved. All exported traces are scrubbed of PII by existing trace exporter filters.

Summary: Introduces a new class of sequential perturbation probes and a pragmatic gate for reducing noisy CI failures while surfacing cascade-sensitive regressions. This fills a gap in our eval coverage and provides actionable signals to triage teams.
review_comments: Diego Martinez (reviewer): Overall looks good. Concern: the adversarial-grid mode can explode combinatorially. Can we add a max-depth and cardinality guard?
Maya Chen (author): Added max_depth and max_branch knobs to the config; default max_depth=3 and cardinality cap=50 in examples/minimality_schedule.yaml.
Lars Håkansson (reviewer): Please add a short circuit for schedules that produce identical outputs after two steps to avoid wasted cycles.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented an identity-check early-exit and added tests to cover it.
Aisha Kapoor (reviewer): Gate scoring looks reasonable but we should surface cohort-level contribution to the severity score in the dashboard.
Maya Chen (author): Dashboard schema updated; trace_exporter now includes cohort_weight in the payload.
CI: initial run failed on lint; fixed import ordering and re-ran. Final CI: all checks passed.

release_notes: Add sequential perturbation probes and a grace-window CI gate to detect cascading prompt regressions while reducing transient flapping. Includes new metrics (compression-aware divergence, token saliency delta) and a CI backfill pipeline. Soft-fail by default; opt-in rollout.
